questions.stem: Which of the following can be an outcome of acute inflammation? Complete resolution Healing by connective tissue replacement Progression to chronic inflammation
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. All 1, 2 and 3

Acute inflammatory reactions typically have one of three outcomes

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about nitric oxide? NO relaxes vascular smooth muscle and cause vasodilation NO helps in generation of free radicals in neutrophil at the time of inflammation Interferon-γ (IFN-γ) or microbial products can activate inducible NOS Synthesis of NO requires NOS action on arginine
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Only 1, 3 and 4

iNOS produces nitric oxide which is mainly useful in inflammation and produced by macrophages (almost nil by neutrophil).

*NO, a soluble gas produced from arginine by the action of nitric oxide synthase (NOS), also participates in microbial killing.

*3 subtypes: eNOS and nNOS are constitutively expressed at low levels, and the NO they generate maintain vascular tone and as a neurotransmitter, respectively.

*iNOS, the type that is involved in microbial killing, is induced when macrophages (and, to a lesser extent, neutrophils) are activated by cytokines (e.g., interferon-γ [IFN-γ]) or microbial products.

*In macrophages, NO reacts with superoxide (O2•) to generate the highly reactive free radical peroxynitrite (ONOO−). These nitrogen-derived free radicals, similar to ROS, attack and damage the lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids of microbes.

*In addition to its role as a microbicidal substance, NO relaxes vascular smooth muscle and promotes vasodilation. It is NOT CLEAR if this action of NO plays an important role in the vascular reactions of acute inflammation.

questions.stem: Which of the following complement component can be activated is both common as well as alternative pathways?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) C3

 

The complement system can be activated via three pathways:

 

  • Classical Pathway – triggered by antigen-antibody complexes
  • Alternative Pathway – triggered directly by pathogen surfaces
  • Lectin Pathway – triggered by mannose-binding lectin (MBL) binding to pathogens

 

C3 is the key point of convergence:

 

  • C3 is the first component common to all three pathways.
  • In the classical and lectin pathways, C3 is activated downstream after C4 and C2 form the C3 convertase (C4b2a).
  • In the alternative pathway, spontaneous hydrolysis of C3 or C3b binding to microbial surfaces initiates activation.
  • In both, C3 is cleaved to C3a and C3b, which drive the complement cascade forward.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. C1: Only involved in the classical pathway.

 

Option B. C2: Used only in the classical and lectin pathways.

 

Option D. C4: Not used in the alternative pathway

questions.stem: A 28-year-old female presents with a butterfly-shaped facial rash, photosensitivity, and joint pain. She reports a history of recurrent oral ulcers and hair loss. Laboratory tests reveal the presence of anti-nuclear antibodies (ANA). Which of the following complement components is often consumed and depleted in this autoimmune condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. C4

The clinical presentation and laboratory findings are suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), an autoimmune disease characterized by the production of autoantibodies against self-antigens, including nuclear antigens. In SLE, the complement system is often activated, leading to consumption and depletion of complement components. One of the most commonly depleted components is C4.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an arachidonic acid metabolite which does not increase inflammation?

Lipoxins A4/B4 are anti-inflammatory molecules as they inhibit neutrophil chemotaxis and adhesion to endothelium.

questions.stem: Which of the following enzymes is involved in the formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. MPO and elastase

 

Neutrophil elastase and MPO help in chromatin decondensation.

 

Neutrophil elastase is a serine protease released by activated neutrophils and is responsible for degrading proteins in the extracellular matrix.

 

  • Option A; ACE is incorrect as it involved in BP regulation through the RAAS.

  • Option C (Pancreatic lipase) is incorrect because it is an enzyme involved in the digestion and breakdown of dietary fats in the small intestine.

  • Option D (Alanine aminotransferase) is incorrect because it is an enzyme primarily found in liver cells and is commonly used as a marker for liver damage in clinical tests. It is not directly involved in NET formation.

  • It is a Beneficial suicide, (Increased risk of SLE and death of concerned neutrophil)

questions.stem: A 65-year-old male smoker presents with a four-day history of cough, fever, and shortness of breath. The cough is productive of yellowish sputum. On physical examination, decreased breath sounds are auscultated on the right lower lung field, and dullness to percussion is noted in the same area. Antibiotics were started by the physician and he stated improving. Which of the following cytokines will most likely be seen in the resolution phase of bacterial pneumonia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans B. IL-10

Anti-inflammatory cytokines predominate in the resolution phase of bacterial pneumonia. Anti-inflammatory cytokines are IL-4, IL-10, IL-13, TGF -beta and Lipoxins

questions.stem: All of the following can lead to mast cell degranulation and histamine release except:

options.label: B
options.text: Binding of antigen to IgE antibodies displayed on the surfaces of mast cells

options.label: C
options.text: Products of complement called anaphylatoxins like C3b and C5b

questions.answerText: Products of complement called anaphylatoxins like C3b and C5b
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Products of complement called anaphylatoxins like C3b and C5b

 

Products of complement called anaphylatoxins like C3a and C5a cause histamine release.

 

  • C3b and C5b are not anaphylatoxins.
  • C3b: Opsonization (helps in phagocytosis)
  • C5b: Part of the membrane attack complex (MAC)
  • The true anaphylatoxins are:
    • -C3a
    • -C4a
    • -C5a
  • These do cause mast cell degranulation, but C3b and C5b do not.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Physical injury (trauma, cold, and heat): True.

 

  • Mast cells can degranulate in response to physical stimuli.
  • This is part of the non-IgE-mediated (or non-immunologic) activation pathway.
  • Temperature extremes and mechanical trauma are known triggers.

 

Option B. Binding of antigen to IgE antibodies displayed on the surfaces of mast cells: True.

 

  • This is the classic Type I hypersensitivity mechanism.
  • Allergen binds to IgE already bound to FcεRI receptors on mast cells → degranulation → release of histamine and other mediators.

 

Option D. Drugs like vancomycin and morphine: True.

 

These drugs can cause non-IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation.

 

For example:

 

  • Vancomycin → “Red man syndrome”
  • Morphine → Flushing, pruritus due to histamine release

questions.stem: A 45-year-old male presents to the clinic with a swollen, painful, and erythematous left leg. He reports a recent history of prolonged immobilization due to a long-haul flight. Physical examination reveals warmth and tenderness over the affected leg. Laboratory tests show an elevated D-dimer level. Which of the following mediators is primarily responsible for initiating the coagulation cascade in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Tissue factor (Factor 7)

Tissue factor is a potent initiator of the coagulation cascade. In response to tissue damage or inflammation, tissue factor is exposed, leading to the activation of Factor VII and subsequent initiation of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. In this patient presenting with signs and symptoms of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) following prolonged immobilization, tissue factor plays a crucial role in triggering the coagulation cascade.

Option B, Plasmin, is involved in fibrinolysis and the breakdown of blood clots. While elevated D-dimer levels suggest ongoing fibrinolysis, the primary mediator responsible for initiating the coagulation cascade in this patient is tissue factor.

Option C, Von Willebrand factor (vWF), is involved in platelet adhesion and aggregation but not in the initiation of the coagulation cascade.

Option D, Thromboxane A2, is a product of arachidonic acid metabolism and promotes platelet aggregation and vasoconstriction but does not directly initiate the coagulation cascade.
